outcome: Need for bag and mask ventilation
cohort: 230 pregnant women in labor with meconium-stained liquor, divided into two groups based on mode of delivery: 115 cesarean deliveries and 115 vaginal deliveries
finding: Vaginal delivery in the presence of meconium-stained liquor was associated with higher incidence of respiratory distress, perinatal asphyxia, NICU admission, meconium aspiration syndrome, and neonatal death.
mod_finding: While there was no significant difference in Apgar scores at 5 minutes between delivery modes, fetal morbidity and mortality were higher in vaginal deliveries.
